title: Components deep dive — content projection, ViewChild, dynamic loading
exp: Standalone components are the standard. But senior interviews test the less-common features: multi-slot content projection, ViewChild for DOM access, TemplateRef for structural patterns, and dynamic component loading with ViewContainerRef. These appear in component library and advanced UI questions.
pts: Standalone components (`standalone: true`, default v19+) import their own dependencies — no NgModule declaration needed
`@Component` metadata: selector, template/templateUrl, styles/styleUrls, changeDetection, encapsulation
**Content projection:** `<ng-content>` projects content from the parent into the child. **Multi-slot:** `<ng-content select="[header]">` projects only elements matching the CSS selector
**`ng-container`:** grouping element that renders no DOM node — useful with `@if` / `@for` to avoid extra wrapper divs
**`ng-template`:** defines a template fragment that is not rendered by default; referenced by `TemplateRef`; used with structural directives and `ViewContainerRef`
**`@ViewChild(ref)`:** queries a child in the current component's VIEW — available in `ngAfterViewInit`. `@ViewChildren` for a list of children.
**`@ContentChild(ref)`:** queries a child projected via `<ng-content>` — available in `ngAfterContentInit`. `@ContentChildren` for a list.
**`ElementRef`:** wraps a native DOM element. Prefer Renderer2 for DOM manipulation to stay cross-platform (SSR/Web Worker safe).
**Dynamic component loading:** `ViewContainerRef.createComponent(ComponentClass)` instantiates a component at runtime — used for modals, toasts, dynamic dashboards
View encapsulation: `Emulated` (default, scoped CSS via attribute), `None` (global CSS), `ShadowDom` (native shadow DOM)
pr: Build a reusable card component with header/body/footer content projection slots

qa.q: What is the difference between @ViewChild and @ContentChild?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** @ViewChild queries elements in the component's own template (its VIEW) — the DOM it creates itself. Available after ngAfterViewInit. @ContentChild queries elements that were PROJECTED into the component via <ng-content> — content that came from the parent. Available after ngAfterContentInit. Practical: @ViewChild for finding a child component you defined in your template; @ContentChild for finding what the parent injected into your slots.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: What is multi-slot content projection and how do you implement it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Multi-slot content projection lets a component define multiple named slots for projected content using CSS selectors on <ng-content>. Add a select attribute: <ng-content select="[header]"> only projects elements with the header attribute, <ng-content select=".footer"> projects elements with the footer CSS class, <ng-content> (no select) is the default slot for everything else. The parent marks its projected elements with the matching attribute or class.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.

qa.q: What is ViewContainerRef and what can you do with it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ViewContainerRef is an injection token representing a position in the DOM where views (component or template instances) can be inserted. You can use it to: createComponent(Type) — dynamically instantiate and insert a component; createEmbeddedView(TemplateRef) — render an ng-template at that position; clear() — remove all dynamically created views. It's the foundation for modals, dynamic dashboards, and structural directives.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

qa.q: What is the difference between ng-container and ng-template?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ng-container renders NO DOM element — it's a logical grouping element for applying @if, @for, or directives without adding a wrapper div. ng-template defines a template fragment that is NOT rendered at all by default — it's a blueprint that must be explicitly instantiated via ngTemplateOutlet, ViewContainerRef.createEmbeddedView(), or a structural directive. Think: ng-container is "invisible wrapper," ng-template is "stored-but-not-rendered blueprint."

qa.q: When would you use ElementRef vs Renderer2 for DOM manipulation?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ElementRef gives you direct access to the native DOM element via nativeElement — simple but platform-specific (breaks in Server-Side Rendering or Web Workers). Renderer2 provides an abstraction layer for DOM manipulation (createElement, setAttribute, setStyle, listen) that works across all Angular platforms including SSR. Use ElementRef for read-only access or when you're certain you're in a browser context; use Renderer2 for all DOM writes to ensure SSR compatibility.
